question: How do I choose a home based on my commute to a base or shipyard?
answer: Drive the real route at your real hours before you offer, including any bridge or tunnel crossings, and time the trip to the gate or work site. Ask coworkers about traffic and gate delays, then weigh the commute against the total cost of the home.
answer_short: Drive the real route at real hours, including water crossings, and time the trip to your gate or site before you offer.
description: How to choose a Hampton Roads home by commute to a base or shipyard: test the drive at your hours, check water crossings, and compare total cost.
body:
Time is money, and a bad commute is a daily tax. Test it for real before you commit.

A Simple Commute Test

  1. Pick your hours. Drive in the morning and evening periods you will actually use.
  2. Include the crossings. Hampton Roads is split by water, so bridges and tunnels can change a trip.
  3. Time it to the gate. Include gate or parking time, not only the drive.
  4. Ask coworkers. People who already commute there know what maps do not show.
  5. Run the full cost. A shorter commute can come with a higher price; compare with the compare tool.

Do not skip the flood and noise checks while you are at it. See mistakes military buyers make.
faqs: Is the shortest commute always the best choice?
Not always. Consider price, flood and noise exposure, and how reliable the route is at your hours.
